episodes.title: The Room of Pictures: Ezekiel 4-8, Job 2, John 7, 2 Peter 1
episodes.summary: Ezekiel 4-8 was taught as the mute prophet's sign-acts and the first temple vision (593-592 B.C., Zedekiah reigning, 8:1 dated the sixth year, sixth month, fifth day). The brick siege drew Calvin's 'childish spectacle, unless God had commanded' and Henry's contrast with Zion on God's palms. The 390 and 40 days (nasa avon) were explained as Jeroboam to the fall plus Judah's last forty years (Calvin, Henry), with Keil's 430 as a new Egypt and Poole's 'God in very deed had patiently borne with them'. The hard question, whether Ezekiel literally lay there, set Calvin (vision only) and Keil's arithmetic (413 versus 437 days) against Henry (real, at set hours); the host sided with Henry. The one New Testament move: Ezekiel displays the burden while Isaiah 53:12 and 1 Peter 2:24 show the one who bears it away (Calvin and Keil: no expiation here). Also covered: the dung bread and Ezekiel's 'Ah, Lord God' as pleading within obedience; the razor and the sifted remnant (Poole); 'This is Jerusalem' at the center of the nations; 6:9 nishbarti 'I have been broken' (Henry's grieved husband, Calvin's two senses); qets and Amos 8:2; and 7:10 'the rod has blossomed' set against Aaron's rod (Calvin: the seed of the staff was their pride). In chapter 8 the four scenes were the image of jealousy (Manasseh's Asherah); the seventy elders in the room of pictures (maskit) with Jaazaniah son of Shaphan, set against Shaphan's godly sons in Jeremiah (Ahikam, Gemariah, Elasah, Gedaliah); 'The Lord does not see us' as complaint not theory (Calvin); Tammuz, the month of 1:1, with Jerome's Bethlehem grove of Adonis (Letter 58); the twenty-five sun-worshipers with backs to the temple, with Mishnah Sukkah 5:4 ('and we, our eyes are to God'); and the branch to the nose left open. Application: let God dig into the hidden room and build a chamber of devotion (Henry paraphrased). Job 2 covered the second council, tummah, hinnam turned back on Satan (Gill, Poole), Gregory on God being 'moved', skin for skin, Deuteronomy 28:35, mud with mud, the wife quoting God's words with Satan's conclusion (Gregory quoted; Spurgeon 3255 gentler, paraphrased), nabal, Henry on good and evil 'from the hand of God', lips versus heart, Teman and Shuah, and the seven days of silence as the friends' best moment. John 7:45-53 covered the officers (Chrysostom 'came back bound themselves by wonder'; Spurgeon 951 'he had fairly taken them'; Calvin 'softened rather than broken' paraphrased), the Pharisees' contempt, Nicodemus (Calvin severe, Augustine kind, Calvin's hidden seed and John 19:39), Jonah of Gath-hepher, Isaiah 9 and Augustine's 'Yet the Lord of the prophets arose thence', and the 7:53-8:11 text question deferred. 2 Peter 1:12-21 covered esterigmenous and sterizo, skenoma and exodos echoing the Transfiguration (Luke 9:31), Calvin's last words as a testament, Piper (1982) 'the difference ... is history', the 'more sure' question (Calvin; Reformation Study Bible; Piper and the ESV, which the host took), auchmeros as squalid, Calvin and Augustine on the day as the last day, William Bridge's 'the more you will lift up your hands and admire', 1:20 as origin not reader, pheromenoi with the voice 'borne' and the ship of Acts 27 (Barnes), and Westminster Confession 1.10. Closing connections: the dark painted room (Ezekiel 8) and the lamp in a squalid place (2 Peter 1:19); the Booths reversal of Ezekiel 8:16 and the officers at that same feast.
threads: Ezekiel 9-12 is next: the man clothed in linen with the writing case marks foreheads of those who sigh and groan (9:4; check whether Cyprian or other fathers read the tav mark as the cross before quoting), judgment beginning at the sanctuary (9:6, already tied to 1 Peter 4:17 in episode 11), the glory moving to the threshold (9:3, 10:4) and leaving to the mountain east of the city (11:23), the cherubim identified (10:20), Jaazaniah son of Azzur and Pelatiah (11:1, 13; Keil distinguishes him from 8:11's son of Shaphan), the 'new heart' promise (11:19), and Ezekiel's baggage sign and covered face (12). Calvin's lectures continue through chapter 20.
The muteness thread (3:26 until 33:22) and the glory arc (1-3 arrives, 8-11 departs, 43 returns, 48:35) continue. Today the glory was still present at 8:4 but 'driven far' (8:6).

Unused Ezekiel 4-8 material: Calvin's prayers at the end of Lectures 11 and 17; Calvin on the iron pan and sacraments needing God's word; Henry's 'fancy is like fire, a good servant, but a bad master', 'Oh that the wickedness of the wicked might come to an end, before it bring them to an end!', 'serve an idol in tears', and 'some hole or other left in the wall'; Gregory the Great's Pastoral Rule on 8:8 ('what is digging in a wall but opening the hardness of the heart by sharp inquisitions?'); Poole on the backs to the temple as 'abrenunciation'; Ligonier 'Learning God's Lessons' on post-exilic monotheism; Gill on the navel of the earth.

Job 3 is next: Job curses the day of his birth, the first poetry of the book, and the first speech after seven days of silence. Henry's 'They were silent, as men astonished and amazed' and Spurgeon 3255's 'Their tender mercies were cruel, though well-intentioned' are unused. Gregory's Moralia Book IV covers Job 3. Unused Job 2: Tertullian's 'How did God smile' (Of Patience 14), Gregory's 'the old enemy was beaten by Adam on a dunghill, he that conquered Adam in Paradise', Gill on Job's wife as normally good.

John 8:1-11 is next: the pericope adulterae and its absence from the earliest manuscripts (the ESV brackets 7:53-8:11); state the Presbyterian and confessional approach to textual criticism briefly (Westminster Confession 1.8) and teach the passage honestly. Augustine's Tractate 33 continues into 8:1-11 ('misery and mercy'). John 8:12 'I am the light of the world' follows, set up today by Isaiah 9:1-2 and Augustine's 'Lord of the prophets', plus the Mishnah Sukkah lamps.

2 Peter 2:1-9 is next: false prophets among the people as false teachers among you (picks up 1:19-21 directly), destructive heresies, denying the Master who bought them, angels cast into Tartarus, Noah a herald of righteousness, Lot righteous and distressed, 'the Lord knows how to rescue the godly'. Unused 2 Peter 1 material: Dever's 'You have to be pretty certain of the truth to die for it' and 'It's no insult to anyone to remind them' (Ligonier, 'Certain Truth'); Piper's 'His bequest to the church is not money' and 'dawn without and daystar within'; Calvin's 'who ruled in their mouth as in his own sanctuary' and 'their doctrine lives and prevails'; Augustine Tractate 35 on lamps.

Voices used this episode: Calvin (Ezekiel 2 quoted, many paraphrased; John and 2 Peter paraphrased), Poole, Henry (2), Jerome, the Mishnah, Gregory the Great, Chrysostom, Spurgeon (951), Augustine, Piper (SermonIndex copy of a 1982 Desiring God sermon), William Bridge, Westminster Confession 1.10; paraphrased Keil and Delitzsch, Gill, Ligonier devotionals, Spurgeon 3255, the Reformation Study Bible, Barnes, Ellicott. No Spurgeon sermon on Ezekiel 4-8 exists in the indexes checked. Desiring God still returns 403. Next time consider Cyprian on the tav mark (Ezekiel 9:4), Owen, Watson, Brooks, Boston, Ryle on John 8, Augustine Tractate 33, Schreiner or MacArthur on 2 Peter 2, and Gregory's Moralia Book IV.

episodes.title: The Mark of the Mourners: Ezekiel 9-12, Job 3, John 8, 2 Peter 2
episodes.summary: Ezekiel 9-12 was taught as the end of the 592 B.C. temple vision and the staged departure of the glory: 9:3 to the threshold, 10:18-19 to the east gate, 11:23 to the Mount of Olives, with Henry's 'God's departures from a people are gradual'. 9:4 covered the man in linen marking those who sigh and groan (ne'enachim, ne'enaqim) and the tav as a signature mark (Job 31:35). Tertullian's cross reading was set against Poole's 'too curious' and Keil's middle way (paraphrased), with Revelation 7:3 as the first New Testament move. The hard question was whether the mark spared the godly; Calvin's answer was that it means separation and God's faithfulness, not immunity from all injury. Also covered: 9:9 quoting 8:12 back at the elders; coals scattered rather than cleansing (Isaiah 6); Calvin on Psalm 132 and the interrupted promise; the cauldron slogan of 11:3 mocking Jeremiah 29, and Riblah; the irony of the names Pelatiah and Benaiah; 'men of your redemption' (11:15) with Calvin on the church in hiding places; miqdash me'at (11:16) with Spurgeon No. 2001's 'travelling temple' and Henry's temple-without-God contrast; and 11:19-20 with Calvin's stone that cannot be inscribed, 2 Corinthians 3:3 as the second New Testament move, Sproul's 'regeneration precedes faith' via Ligonier, and Westminster Confession 10. Ezekiel 12 covered the baggage sign (digging through the wall echoing 8:8) and Zedekiah 'shall not see it', with Josephus on Zedekiah disbelieving both prophets, and the two proverbs of delay (Henry paraphrased). Application: be a mourner, not a commentator. Job 3 covered the switch to poetry and the three movements, with Trapp's 'Diem, non Deum'. Qalal was set against barak, then came Genesis 1 reversed (Ash), Sheol as rest, and the hedge of 3:23 against 1:10 (Poole). The 'did Job sin' question was answered with Calvin's 'mixture' (paraphrased from his sermons) and Poole: no blasphemy, but real infirmity. The segment also covered the parallel with Jeremiah 20, a pastoral word on despair, and Derek Thomas's 'utterly honest'. John 7:53-8:11 addressed the textual question with Westminster Confession 1.8, Calvin's 'nothing unworthy of an Apostolic Spirit' and Carson (paraphrased). It then covered the trap and the missing man, the views on what Jesus wrote (Augustine, Ambrose and Jerome on Jeremiah 17:13, Calvin), Deuteronomy 17:7 with Sproul, conviction versus repentance (Calvin), Augustine's 'the wretched woman and Mercy', Henry's 'I do forgive thee', and MacArthur on the cross. 2 Peter 2:1-9 covered pareisago, plastos and emporeuomai (the Master bought them; they sell you) and 'their destruction is not asleep'. On 2:1 and definite atonement it gave Gill's 'the Father' view (Deuteronomy 32:6), then Poole's visible-church reading (quoted), Schreiner and Owen paraphrased, Westminster Confession 8.8 and Thomas Adams. It finished with the four-part 'if' and 'then' (Jude contrasted), Clement of Rome on Noah preaching repentance, and Lot as righteous through imputed righteousness, with his ongoing grief as the evidence. Closing connections: the ESV cross-reference from 2 Peter 2:8 to Ezekiel 9:4 (mourners, Lot, and the gleeful accusers of John 8), and the delay proverb of Ezekiel 12:22 answered by 2 Peter 2:3.
threads: Ezekiel 13-15 is next: false prophets who whitewash a wall (13:10-16), the women who sew magic bands, elders with idols in their hearts (14:3), Noah, Daniel and Job (14:14, 20), and the useless vine (15). Job was named today, so link Ezekiel 14:14 to the Job readings. Keep tracking the glory arc: it left to the Mount of Olives at 11:23 and returns by the east gate in 43:1-5. The muteness (3:26 until 33:22) continues. Calvin's lectures run through chapter 20.

Unused Ezekiel 9-12 material: Henry's 'Here the honours of the pen exceeded those of the sword', his note that the man in linen 'reported his matter' while the destroyers did not, 'God will set a mark upon his mourners, will book their sighs and bottle their tears', and 'Perhaps it was Ezekiel's infirmity to bewail the death of this wicked prince'. Calvin's 'For they sin doubly' (9:6), 'fell upon his face as a mediator' (9:8), 'unbelievers turn the patience of God into material for obduracy' (12:22), 'we must still go on, although success does not answer to our labor' (12:3), God as hunter with hidden nets (12:13), and the 'half of God's covenant' warning (11:19-20). Gill's rabbinic ten removes of the Shekinah (Rosh Hashanah 31a) and the Targum's synagogues reading of 11:16. Ellicott on the mark referring 'wholly and only to character'. The Pulpit Commentary naming Jeremiah, Baruch, Ahikam and Gedaliah among the marked. Spurgeon No. 2001's 'The Holy of Holies was great for holiness, but not for space'. Spurgeon's 'The Heart of Flesh' sermon is saved for Ezekiel 36:26.

Job 4 is next: Eliphaz the Temanite speaks first, the night vision (4:12-21), and 'who that was innocent ever perished?' (4:7). Unused Job 3 material: Gregory's 'closed vessels' and 'Adam was created, but Cain was the first man that was born', Trapp's 'never hath any yet been heard to curse the day of his new birth', Caryl's 'Troubles will make a man Rhetoricall' and 'Plenty of sorrow makes a scarcity of words', Ishodad of Merv on grief without blasphemy, Henry's Concise 'willing to die... willing to live', Spurgeon No. 2666's 'not with a hedge of roses, but with a barrier of briars', and Poole on 3:23. Note the qalal bookend with 40:4 'I am of small account' for when Job answers God.

John 8:12-20 is next: 'I am the light of the world' at Booths, with the Mishnah Sukkah lamps lighting every courtyard (fetched in earlier research), Isaiah 9:1-2 and Augustine's 'Lord of the prophets' from episode 15, the testimony of two witnesses, and 'in the treasury' (8:20). Unused 8:1-11 material: Ambrose Letter 26 ('in the remission of sins no man can participate with Christ'), Bengel ('He does not add, in peace'), Lightfoot's bitter-water analogy, Ryle on conscience and on the text, Sproul's 'clothed us with the cloak of His righteousness', and Augustine's account of the passage being removed from manuscripts.

2 Peter 2:10-16 is next: despising authority, blaspheming the glorious ones, 'irrational animals', 'eyes full of adultery', and Balaam's donkey. Unused 2:1-9 material: Owen's 'no purchase mentioned... but a deliverance', Adams's two arms of God and 'Just Lot was delivered, neither for his justice, nor without it', Spurgeon No. 2441's 'it is better that He should know than that we should know', Calvin's 'kept to be punished' and his note on Tartarus sobriety, 1 Clement 11 on Lot's hospitality, and Ligonier's 'Jesus buys false teachers only in that He incorporates them into the visible church'.

Voices quoted this episode: Henry (2), Tertullian, Poole (2), Calvin (3), Spurgeon (No. 2001), Josephus, Trapp, Derek Thomas, Augustine, and Clement of Rome. Paraphrased: Keil and Delitzsch, Gill, Ligonier (Sproul), Christopher Ash, Carson, MacArthur, Sproul, Ambrose, Jerome, Schreiner, Owen, Thomas Adams, and Westminster Confession 1.8, 8.8 and 10. Desiring God still returns 403, so no Piper. Next time consider Caryl, Gregory's Moralia on Job 4, Ryle and Chrysostom on John 8:12, Calvin's lectures on Ezekiel 13-14, Manton or Adams on 2 Peter 2:10-16, and Bunyan or Watson.
